answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable history instead of a free account: an agent must forge a track record of useful, attested work over time before it gains voting weight, so spawning thousands of clones costs more than it earns. Peers then mirror that history publicly, and any identity whose record looks like a lotus blooming overnight — perfect, sudden, with no roots — is quarantined for review rather than trusted.
